```{r Step 1, BLS Ingestion, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# BLS_Ingest.Rmd
# Precariat Politics
#
# BLS data for externally measured job quality
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Analysis period
# ------------------------------------------------------------

BLS_START_YEAR <- 2000
BLS_END_YEAR   <- 2024


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. API key
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# blsR will automatically use BLS_API_KEY from .Renviron
# if it has been set there.

if (Sys.getenv("BLS_API_KEY") == "") {

  warning(
    paste(
      "BLS_API_KEY not detected.",
      "The BLS API can still be queried, but requests",
      "will be subject to stricter limits."
    )
  )

} else {

  message("BLS API key detected.")

}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create BLS directories
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dir.create(
  here::here("00_rawdata", "BLS_Data"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  here::here("01_tidydata", "BLS_Data"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# PART I
# EMPLOYER COSTS / BENEFITS
# ============================================================

# ECEC series use the CM prefix.
#
# The industry codes include:
#
# 5100 = Information
# 5200 = Finance and insurance
# 5300 = Real estate and rental and leasing
# 5400 = Professional, scientific, and technical services
#
# Estimate codes include:
#
# 01 = Total compensation
# 02 = Wages and salaries
# 03 = Total benefits
# 04 = Paid leave
# 13 = Insurance
# 15 = Health insurance
# 18 = Retirement and savings
#
# We will pull these first and determine which ones are
# sufficiently comparable over the full study period.


ecec_series <- c(

  # Information
  information_total_compensation =
    "CMU2X0000051000D",
  information_wages =
    "CMU2X0000051000D",
  information_benefits =
    "CMU2X0000051000D",

  # Finance and insurance
  finance_total_compensation =
    "CMU2X0000052000D",
  finance_wages =
    "CMU2X0000052000D",
  finance_benefits =
    "CMU2X0000052000D",

  # Real estate
  real_estate_total_compensation =
    "CMU2X0000053000D",
  real_estate_wages =
    "CMU2X0000053000D",
  real_estate_benefits =
    "CMU2X0000053000D",

  # Professional / scientific / technical
  professional_technical_total_compensation =
    "CMU2X0000054000D",
  professional_technical_wages =
    "CMU2X0000054000D",
  professional_technical_benefits =
    "CMU2X0000054000D"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Do NOT run the ECEC block above until we verify the exact
# series IDs against the current BLS series structure.
#
# The ECEC series-ID architecture is documented here:
#
# https://www.bls.gov/ecec/factsheets/ecec-series-id-guide.htm
#
# I am deliberately leaving this block as a series map rather
# than silently treating these constructed IDs as verified.
#
# We will populate the exact IDs after inspecting the BLS
# series definitions.
# ------------------------------------------------------------


# ============================================================
# PART II
# JOLTS TURNOVER
# ============================================================

# JOLTS provides industry-level:
#
#   - hires
#   - quits
#   - layoffs/discharges
#   - total separations
#
# For our eventual job-quality measure, quits and total
# separations are particularly useful as indicators of
# employment mobility/turnover.
#
# We will use NOT SEASONALLY ADJUSTED annual data and
# aggregate monthly observations to the annual level.


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Example: retrieve a JOLTS series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# IMPORTANT:
# Exact series IDs should be verified from the current JOLTS
# series documentation before building the final industry map.


# ============================================================
# PART III
# OEWS / OCCUPATIONAL WAGES
# ============================================================

# OEWS provides occupational employment and wage estimates.
#
# This is particularly useful because our GSS data contain
# OCC10, while the GSS prestige measure is occupation-based.
#
# The eventual goal is to construct an occupation-level
# component that can complement the industry-level BLS data.


# ============================================================
# PART IV
# SAVE RAW BLS DATA
# ============================================================

# Raw API results will be saved under:
#
# 00_rawdata/BLS_Data/
#
# Cleaned / harmonized versions will eventually go under:
#
# 01_tidydata/BLS_Data/


message("")
message("====================================================")
message("BLS INGESTION ENVIRONMENT READY")
message("====================================================")
message(
  "Analysis period: ",
  BLS_START_YEAR,
  "–",
  BLS_END_YEAR
)
message("")
message(
  "Next step: verify BLS series IDs before pulling",
  "the complete benefits and turnover panel."
)
message("====================================================")
```
